title: Prod uptime monitor has not run since 2026-10-28T21:11Z; its last run misread HTTP 429 as an outage and could not send the alert
failure_scenario: Prod goes down (as on 2026-07-12) and nobody hears about it: the only probe of the public hostname is not running, and Railway's own dashboards stay green when only the Cloudflare layer breaks. It has been in this state for about 3 days. When it does run, a Cloudflare rate-limit (429) on Railway's shared egress IP raises a false 'DOWN, redeploy the Worker' alert, and the same rate-limit blocks that alert from reaching the relay.

title: One credential can both read and delete every prod DB backup; no object lock or versioning, and the R2 keys were in the 2026-10-21 Railway env exposure
location: backup/backup.sh:97-111; backup/Dockerfile:15; infra/terraform/environments/experiment-backups/main.tf:33-36,54-61,96-104; docs/backups-cloud-runbook.md:11-17; Railway pg-r2-backup (3224fca5-f6cc-47f9-8dba-6b1db81fda1c) vars R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
failure_scenario: Anyone holding the leaked or still-unrotated backup key can download all 30 full prod dumps (customers, orders, financials) and then delete them. A compromised Railway env or bad run can also prune every dump. Either way, no offsite copy is left for the next data-loss incident.

title: Merging to main deploys the prod backend (and runs its migrations) without waiting for CI; no branch protection requires a check
location: Railway backend service 26d2f448-d4f2-4f67-b2ef-1628ef27a5c0 source.checkSuites=false (production/main and dev/dev); GitHub branch protection main+dev required_status_checks=null; .github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:11-13; apps/backend/Dockerfile:68
failure_scenario: A release whose main merge ref fails typecheck or the backend suite (a hotfix on main that dev lacks, a bad merge resolution, or a PR merged while red) deploys to prod anyway. Its migrations run against the prod database before anyone sees the red check, and migrations cannot be rolled back.

title: [cross-lane] Nightly prod-to-dev db-sync has failed every night since 2026-10-28, with no alert
location: deploy/railway-sync/scrub.sql:32-45 (generic *_enc nulling); apps/backend/migrations/0213_fleet_proxies.sql:14 (url_enc TEXT NOT NULL); deploy/railway-sync/sync.sh:111-116; Railway dev db-sync 006cd405-7bee-4a66-8ebc-6ca6fdaa44ad deployment 5fecc5a6 (status SUCCESS)
failure_scenario: Dev stays frozen at the 2026-10-27 prod copy. Data-migration dry runs and QA on dev then test against a stale schema and data shape while everyone assumes it refreshes nightly. The failure is visible only in logs.

title: Prod backend watch patterns leave out root manifests, unlike dev; neither environment watches pnpm-workspace.yaml
location: Railway backend production build.watchPatterns=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**]; dev=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.base.json]; pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-21; .github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:36-43
failure_scenario: A lockfile- or override-only security fix (e.g. a nodemailer refresh, see A11-09) merges to main. Prod backend is not rebuilt and keeps the vulnerable dependency until some unrelated backend change triggers a deploy. Dev, which watches the lockfile, gets the fix, so a check on dev wrongly suggests prod has it too.
